'''Paul Finsler''' (11 April 1894 – 29 April 1970) was a German and Swiss [[mathematician]].<ref name="sta">{{MacTutor|id=Finsler|title=Paul Finsler}}</ref>

Born in [[Heilbronn]], [[German Empire|Germany]], Finsler did his undergraduate studies at the [[University of Stuttgart|Technische Hochschule Stuttgart]],<ref name="sta"/> and his graduate studies at the [[University of Göttingen]], where he received his Ph.D. in 1919 under the supervision of [[Constantin Carathéodory]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Paul Finsler|id=52428}}.</ref> He studied for his [[habilitation]] at the [[University of Cologne]], receiving it in 1922.<ref name="sta"/> He joined the faculty of the [[University of Zurich]] in 1927, and was promoted to [[ordinary professor]] there in 1944.<ref name="sta"/> He died on 29 April 1970.

Finsler's thesis work concerned [[differential geometry]], and [[Finsler manifold|Finsler spaces]] were named after him by [[Élie Cartan]] in 1934.<ref name="sta"/> The [[Hadwiger–Finsler inequality]], a relation between the side lengths and area of a [[triangle]] in the [[Euclidean plane]], is named after Finsler and his co-author [[Hugo Hadwiger]], as is the [[Finsler–Hadwiger theorem]] on a square derived from two other squares that share a vertex.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Finsler | first1 = Paul
 | last2 = Hadwiger | first2 = Hugo | author2-link = Hugo Hadwiger
 | doi = 10.1007/BF01214300
 | issue = 1
 | journal = [[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]]
 | pages = 316–326
 | title = Einige Relationen im Dreieck
 | volume = 10
 | year = 1937| s2cid = 122841127
 }}.</ref> Finsler is also known for his work on the [[foundations of mathematics]], developing a [[non-well-founded set theory]] with which he hoped to resolve the contradictions implied by [[Russell's paradox]].<ref name="sta"/><ref>{{citation
 | last = Breger | first = Herbert
 | contribution = A restoration that failed: Paul Finsler's theory of sets
 | editor-last = Gillies | editor-first = Donald
 | pages = 249–264
 | publisher = Oxford University Press
 | title = Revolutions in Mathematics
 | year = 1992| title-link = Revolutions in Mathematics
 }}.</ref>
